newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- Stock prices rose to new highs on Thursday.
- Figures released on Thursday show a strong economy, flush consumers and a resilient bull market were not enough to give American retailers the 1996 holiday season they wanted.
- The two bids for the military businesses of Hughes Electronics are likely to come to some $10 billion.
- Producer prices rose more than expected during December.

- Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group, which shocked the rest of the tobacco industry last March by breaking ranks and agreeing to settle several major lawsuits, is now trying to reach an even broader settlement.
- The FAA found problems with ValuJet's system for assuring the safety of its planes as recently as December.
- Mechanics for United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, rejected a wage increase proposal, but other workers accepted the plan.
- Norfolk Southern lost a bid to have a court strike down an agreement that prevents Conrail from discussing a merger with anyone other than CSX Corp.
- Telefonos de Mexico plans to seek authorisation with the FCC to offer its own telephone services in United States markets that are heavily Spanish-speaking.
- Nasdaq said it had scaled back its proposal to reduce the minimum number of shares that can be traded under the SEC's new order-handling rules.
- Behind the success of the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars is a business structure that has helped the new team compete against more established franchises.
